extracted.intended_audience: Clinicians, medical students, and researchers (ATSU-affiliated authors) preparing clinical case reports for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and structuring medical case report manuscripts according to the CARE checklist so they are accurate, transparent, and useful for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of CARE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines must be cited in your references. CARE checklist. https://www.care-statement.org/checklist. Published 2013. Accessed 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the CARE guideline citation in the manuscript references to acknowledge use of the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the diagnosis and the words "case report"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the title explicit about the diagnosis and label the article as a case report to aid discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 2-5 keywords associated with the diagnosis or intervention; include "case report"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select concise, relevant keywords (2–5) that reflect the diagnosis/intervention and label the article type to improve indexing and searchability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (structured, no references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract (Does not include references). Introduction: What is unique about this case? What does it add to scientific literature? Main symptoms and/or important clinical findings. The main diagnosis, therapeutic interventions and outcomes. Conclusion: What is the main "take-away?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief structured abstract that summarizes uniqueness, key findings (symptoms/diagnosis), interventions and outcomes, and a succinct take-away; do not include references in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: One - two paragraphs summarizing the uniqueness of this case (may include references)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the case is noteworthy and how it adds to the literature; keep to one or two paragraphs and cite relevant background literature as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient information
rubrics_metrics.description: De-identified patient specific information; Primary patient related concerns and symptoms; Relevant past medical history (include family and psycho-social); Relevant past interventions with outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient de-identified demographic and clinical background so readers understand the patient's presentation and relevant history, including prior treatments and social/family context where pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant physical examination and clinical findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report key examination findings and objective clinical signs that informed diagnosis and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and current information related to this case
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a clear timeline of events (symptom onset, investigations, interventions, follow-up) to help readers understand the sequence and temporal relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic assessment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the diagnostic work-up (tests, imaging, labs), note any challenges or differential diagnoses considered, and include the expected prognosis based on findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of therapeutic intervention; Administration of intervention; Changes of intervention with rationale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what was done (medical, surgical, preventive), how interventions were administered (dose, timing, technique), and why changes were made, providing clinical rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinician and patient-assessed outcomes; Important follow-up test results; Intervention adherence and tolerance; Adverse or unanticipated events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report objective and subjective outcomes during follow-up, including test results, adherence/tolerance information, and any adverse or unexpected events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengths and limitations related to this case; Discussion of relevant medical literature with references; Scientific rationale for any conclusions (include assessment of possible causes); Primary "take-away" lessons (one paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the case in context with existing literature, candidly discuss strengths and limitations, provide scientific reasoning for conclusions (including possible etiologies), and end with a concise paragraph summarizing the primary lesson(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient impressions of treatment (one - two paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available and appropriate, include 1–2 paragraphs of the patient's own perspective on their care and outcomes to add depth and patient-centered context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the patient provide informed consent? Was consent requested?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether informed consent for publication was obtained from the patient (or legally authorized representative) and document how consent was managed.
